data.source_title: Does health information technology improve acknowledgement of radiology results for discharged Emergency Department patients? A before and after study
data.source_period: One month before and one month after eRA implementation; dates not stated in inspected abstract
data.quantity: Documented acknowledgement of radiology reports for discharged ED patients
data.source_evidence_basis: Original full text XML reports pre period 70.6% (1,167/1,654), post period 100% (1,423/1,423), and calls the increase 30.4 percentage points (95% CI 28.1–32.6). The reported pre/post percentages imply 29.4 percentage points, so the source delta conflicts arithmetically; retain both statements and block quantitative calibration.
data.limitations: Uncontrolled before-after study. The published 30.4 percentage-point increase conflicts with its rounded rates (100.0−70.6=29.4); acknowledgment measures receipt, not interpretation, appropriate action, or patient notification.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Track receipt acknowledgment separately from interpretation, action, and patient contact; exclude reported change magnitude from calibration until source discrepancy is resolved.
